_comment: SAST gate policy. This file is consumed by scripts/sast.sh (it is NOT a gosec -conf file). The blocking gate runs ONLY the high-signal rules in block_rules and requires ZERO findings: every real finding is fixed, every justified exception carries a dedicated '// #nosec Gxxx -- <reason>' comment. -nosec-require-rules and -nosec-require-justification make a bare or reason-less #nosec fail the gate. Every OTHER gosec rule still runs in the informational full scan (task security:report -> docs/security/gate-report.md) so nothing is invisible; it is just not release-blocking. Per-class rationale: docs/security/SECURITY-GATE.md.

block_rules_rationale.G201,G202: SQL built with string formatting/concatenation (SQL injection).
block_rules_rationale.G203: Template method that does not auto-escape HTML (template/XSS injection).
block_rules_rationale.G204: Subprocess launched with a variable (command injection).
block_rules_rationale.G107: HTTP request to a URL taken from a variable (SSRF).
block_rules_rationale.G401,G404: Weak cryptographic primitive / weak (non-crypto) RNG in a security context.

excluded_from_block_note: Rules NOT in block_rules (e.g. G101 name-matched credentials, G104 unhandled errors, G115/G703/G705 integer-overflow-on-conversion, G304 file-path-from-variable, G301/G302/G306 file permissions, G103 unsafe.Pointer) are high-false-positive in this tree and are non-blocking. Their real-risk counterparts are covered elsewhere: gitleaks (task lint:secrets) + the no-secrets-in-logs invariant for credentials; the plugin/rich-doc sandboxes for hostile path handling; go vet + review for error discipline. They remain visible in the informational full scan.
